items.interference: Finance returned HTTP 200 from /readiness when its D1 binding was absent, allowing an unavailable Finance data path to look ready.
items.correction: Finance /readiness now returns 503 whenever D1 is absent or the module is not active; /health remains a liveness endpoint.

items.interference: An unexpected exception from the Identity resolver could escape the Finance gateway path instead of producing a controlled dependency failure.
items.correction: The Finance mount now returns 503 IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE and does not invoke Finance; unrelated gateway mounts continue normally.

items.interference: The Finance D1 integration test imported miniflare without declaring it in the module, and the release workflow ran Finance tests before installing module dependencies.
items.correction: Finance now pins miniflare in devDependencies with a committed lockfile, the Finance deployment workflow installs the locked dependencies before source validation, and the Finance test command has a bounded per-test timeout.

coverageGaps.gap: After its dependency was installed, the full Finance Miniflare D1 integration suite did not complete within the 120-second local execution limit. The focused Finance edge tests and the local chaos D1 readiness scenario pass.
coverageGaps.nextStep: Diagnose Miniflare/workerd startup in an isolated Linux CI job with bounded per-test timeouts; retain the suite as a required Finance gate only after it has a reproducible completion signal.

coverageGaps.gap: CRM aggregate /readiness currently confirms PostgreSQL configuration rather than a live bounded SELECT 1. The suite validates transaction rollback with a failing pool but does not inject a production CRM process fault.
coverageGaps.nextStep: Add a separately pooled, bounded PostgreSQL readiness probe and execute it first in isolated staging; do not make the production health path depend on an unbounded connection attempt.

coverageGaps.gap: No deployed queue consumer is registered for the transactional outbox yet; the suite verifies that a queue outage cannot block the producer, not end-to-end retry/DLQ delivery.
coverageGaps.nextStep: When the first consumer is deployed, add staging-only retry, dead-letter and reconciliation evidence before enabling its flag.
